thread_text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — region=gcp-asia-east1 — GPU node provisioning failing, autoscaler stuck in PREP state. Queue length for hosted-api-inference has gone from ~200 -> 2.4k in 6m. Severity: P0.

maya: Acknowledged. I'm oncall. Quick hit: which models impacted and is there a visible error from the autoscaler?

incident-bot: Models: rdx-1b, rdx-3b, rdx-8b-quant are all served in this region. Autoscaler logs show repeated quota-denied responses from GCP: 
```
ERROR provisioning: quotaExceeded: unable to create instances for project: REGION_QUOTA_EXCEEDED (GPUS_PER_PROJECT_DEFAULT)
```

maya: OK. That matches the quota hit pattern. First goal: limit customer impact. Priorities: 1) stop further queue growth, 2) failover critical routes to us-central1, 3) enable degraded-mode (cpu fallback) for non-critical tenants.

raul: I can take the reroute. Switching route-policy now for production/hosted-api -> prefer: us-central1, fallback: europe-west1. Will it require token pinning changes?

maya: No token pinning changes if we set region preference at route layer. Raul, trigger the route change and post confirmation. Priya, can infra start a quota increase request with GCP support and meanwhile spin up reserved warm-pool from preemptible spare in ap-southeast?

priya: Filing GCP escalation — ticket created 174534-asia-quota. Also starting warm-pool boot in ap-southeast1 with lower-capacity VMs to take lower-priority traffic. Won't take >10m to get a few nodes.

jin: On the autoscaler side I see the controller is hitting a hard cap for GPUs/project in that org. I can flip per-cluster fairshare to deprioritize non-prod and system jobs so we reclaim slot for hosted-api. Doing that now.

leah: Customer impact check — which customers are in the hosted-api region? I'm pulling the list and will draft a short status message for CS.

maya: Good. For immediate mitigation: 1) Raul, do the region reroute. 2) Jin, apply fairshare deprioritization and reduce burstquota for batch workloads. 3) Priya, warm-pool spin. 4) Leah, customer comms: note degraded latency and partial failovers.

raul: Route change command executed: 
```
redwood route update --service hosted-api --region-preference us-central1,europe-west1 --apply
```
Routing logs: 200 OK. Starting traffic shift (gradual 20% step every 30s).

incident-bot: routing: shift-started, step=1/5, moved ~18% of session token traffic. Queue growth rate slowed slightly.

jin: fairshare tweak applied: 
```
kubectl annotate hpa hosted-api fairshare=high:0.6,nonprod:0.1
```
Preemptible reclaim started. Observed ~220 GPUs freed within a minute (system jobs evicted).

maya: Good. Priya any ETA on warm-pool nodes?

priya: Warm-pool boots started. Preemptible nodes in ap-southeast1 showing as ready in ~6m. Created warmpool label and attached to hosted-api autoscaler as burst-pool. Not ideal but reduces latency for lower-priority.

leah: Draft for CS: "We detected capacity constraints in gcp-asia-east1 causing higher latencies and partial request reroutes to alternate regions. We are actively mitigating by diverting traffic and provisioning extra capacity. Some customers will see elevated latency up to ~10s for in-region calls; error rate is low but increased for tail requests. Will update in 30m."

customer-ops: Please include whether any customers have requests pinned to the region — we have one enterprise tenant on reserved capacity here.

maya: Good catch. That reserved tenant is "AcmeHealth"; their traffic is pinned. Priya, can you check dedicated-reservations for AcmeHealth and see if we can temporarily lift the reservation or move their capacity to a different pool?

priya: Checking reservations... AcmeHealth has a dedicated pool in ap-east1-bound to their private deployment. Can't move that easily. I'll open a cherrypick: can we failover their routing to a dedicated standby in us-central?

raul: I can patch their routing config but need ops approval. Maya, approve manual failover for AcmeHealth? It will change their region and could have slight compliance implications.

maya: Approve for mitigation; flag for post-incident review. Leah, notify AcmeHealth via CS that we will perform a temporary region failover.

incident-bot: autoscaler: provision attempts now returning 403/quota for new GPU allocations. WARMPool nodes are used for lower-priority — reduction in queue backlog for those jobs. Overall queue now at ~900 (down from 2.4k).

jin: Observability check: per-route latency graph shows p95 in asia-east1 up to 6.2s, global average p95 2.1s. Error rate 5xx increased from 0.03% -> 0.5% for the region. Logging shows increased KV cache misses as sessions move regions.

leah: Customer comms sent to AcmeHealth and affected midsize tenants. CS asked for ETA — advise 30-45m before stable routing as warm-pool scales and fairshare settles.

maya: Next steps: 1) maintain reroute until quota increase confirmed or warm-pool stable 2) follow up with GCP for quota bump 3) run postmortem on why autoscaler didn't preemptively shift workloads. Assigning tasks: Jin (autoscaler logs + PR to prevent PREP state), Priya (quota escalation + warmpool), Raul (routing sweep), Leah (customer updates + incident postmortem writeup).

raul: Rolled the final step of routing - 100% shift for non-pinned tokens completed at +18m. Pinned tokens remain in asia-east1.

incident-bot: monitor: queue length steady ~820 -> slowly declining. Warm-pool utilization 72%. GPUs provisioned in other regions increased by 310.

priya: GCP escalation replied: can grant temporary quota increase, pending verification. Provided a tentative +200 GPU quota in 25-40m if we pass billing/account verification. Chasing phone line now.

jin: Found a bug in cluster-provisioner that retries on quota errors indefinitely without fallback to other regions — opened hotfix branch and patch is small. Will deploy to controller-manager in 10m.

maya: Deploy patch after quick test. Also note: add auto-fallback to different region on repeated quota errors as a safety rule.

leah: Posting short status in #general and tagging impacted customers. Will schedule postmortem page after incident stabilizes.

customer-ops: AcmeHealth acknowledged failover consent. They confirm temporary routing is acceptable for up to 2h.

raul: Hotfix deployed to autoscaler controller-manager. Observed controller now treats repeated quota failures as transient and triggers regional fallback.

incident-bot: controller: fallback-triggered -> nu-regions: us-central1,europe-west1. Queue now 420 and trending down. Error rate back to ~0.08%.

maya: Great work. Keeping this open for follow-ups and postmortem. If queue <200 and error rate stable for 10m, we'll transition to monitoring and hand off to SRE backlog.

leah: Marking incident mitigated for paging. Postmortem owners: maya (lead), jin (autoscaler), priya (quota/infra), raul (routing), leah (customer comms). ETA for postmortem draft: 3 business days.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated -> paging cleared. :white_check_mark:
